## Introduction

**dimsprepr** provides a complete, reproducible preprocessing pipeline for
direct-injection mass spectrometry (DIMS) metabolomics data. It covers
missing-value filtering, imputation, QC-based signal-drift and batch
correction, normalization, transformation, quality filtering, and scaling,
all orchestrated through a single function call.

## The example data

```{r setup}
library(dimsprepr)

data(dims_data)
data(dims_metadata)

dim(dims_data)
table(dims_metadata$Group, dims_metadata$Batch)
head(dims_metadata)
```

`dims_data` is a simulated 60-injection, 80-feature matrix in two batches.
Pooled QC samples open and close each batch and recur every 6th injection,
the layout QC-based drift correction needs. Zeros mark values below the
detection limit.

## Run the full pipeline

`run_DIpreprocess()` executes all steps in a fixed, validated order:

1. input validation, 2. outlier removal, 3. missing-value filtering,
4. imputation, 5. drift/batch correction (QCRSC), 6. normalization,
7. transformation, 8. quality filtering (QC-RSD and variance, on unscaled
data), 9. scaling into a NONPLS and a PLS branch, 10. replicate merging.

```{r pipeline}
result <- run_DIpreprocess(
  x                = dims_data,
  metadata         = dims_metadata,
  normalize_method = "pqn_group",
  transform_method = "log10",
  spline_smooth    = 0.5,
  verbose          = FALSE
)

result
summary(result)
```

The result keeps the data after each step, the final matrices for the two
scaling branches, and a log of the dimensions:

```{r inspect}
dim(result$data_nonpls)   # auto-scaled: PCA, clustering, univariate tests
dim(result$data_pls)      # Pareto-scaled: PLS-DA / OPLS-DA
head(result$features_final)
```

## Diagnostic plots

`plot_beforeafter()` shows features along the injection order, with a
LOESS trend through the QC samples. Given a pipeline result, it compares
the imputed data with the drift-corrected data:

```{r plot-drift}
plot_beforeafter(result, plot_what = c("mz_0002", "mz_0015"))
```

`plot_dist_beforeafter()` compares distributions, here imputed versus the
final auto-scaled data:

```{r plot-dist}
invisible(plot_dist_beforeafter(result, n_random = 20))
```

## Using individual functions

Each step is also available as a standalone function.

```{r steps}
filt  <- run_filtermissing(dims_data, dims_metadata, threshold = 0.2,
                           verbose = FALSE)
imp   <- run_mvimpute(filt$data, method = 0.2, verbose = FALSE)
corr  <- run_driftBatchCorrect(imp$data, dims_metadata,
                               spline_smooth_param = 0.5, verbose = FALSE)
norm  <- run_normalize(corr$data, dims_metadata, method = "pqn_group",
                       verbose = FALSE)
rsd   <- run_filterRSD(norm$data, dims_metadata, max_rsd = 0.3, verbose = FALSE)
trans <- run_transform(rsd$data, method = "log10", verbose = FALSE)
varf  <- run_filtervariance(trans$data, percentile = 10, verbose = FALSE)
sc    <- run_scale(varf$data, method = "auto", verbose = FALSE)

filt
rsd
sc
```

Note that `run_filtermissing()` converts zeros to `NA` before filtering, and
`run_mvimpute()` imputes only `NA` values.

## Comparing preprocessing strategies

Supply vectors to `normalize_method`, `transform_method`, `scale_nonpls`, or
`scale_pls` to compute all combinations. Steps 1 to 5 run only once, and
normalization, transformation, and filtering run once per
normalize x transform pair:

```{r multi}
multi <- run_DIpreprocess(
  x                = dims_data,
  metadata         = dims_metadata,
  normalize_method = c("median", "pqn_group"),
  transform_method = c("log10", "glog"),
  spline_smooth    = 0.5,
  verbose          = FALSE
)
multi
```
